name: GlyNAC
summary: Glycine + NAC combo with small trials on glutathione and aging markers.
lead: GlyNAC is a combination of two amino acids, glycine and N-acetylcysteine (NAC, a precursor of cysteine), that are the building blocks limiting the body's synthesis of the antioxidant tripeptide glutathione. It is sold over the counter as a dietary supplement and has been studied mainly as an intervention for age-related glutathione deficiency, oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction.

name: Alpha-ketoglutarate
summary: Metabolic intermediate investigated in aging biology. Preliminary.
lead: Alpha-ketoglutarate (AKG, also 2-oxoglutarate) is an organic acid that occurs naturally in the body as an intermediate of the citric acid cycle and as a hub linking energy metabolism with amino acid and nitrogen handling. It is also sold as an over-the-counter supplement, usually as a calcium salt, and has attracted interest in longevity circles.

name: Caffeine (topical)
summary: Constricts vessels for a temporary under-eye depuff.
lead: Topical caffeine refers to caffeine, the xanthine alkaloid found in coffee and tea, formulated at low concentrations in creams, serums and gels. It appears in many under-eye products marketed to reduce puffiness and dark circles.

name: Hesperidin
summary: Vein-supporting flavonoid used for venous and microvascular issues.
lead: Hesperidin is a flavanone glycoside found in citrus fruits, concentrated in the white inner peel; its aglycone is hesperetin. It was first isolated in 1828 by the French chemist M. Lebreton. It is sold as a dietary supplement, often combined with diosmin or vitamin C, in products aimed at venous and capillary complaints.

name: Dandelion extract
summary: Marketed herbal diuretic. Weak evidence.
lead: Dandelion extract is a preparation from the leaves, roots or flowers of Taraxacum officinale, the common dandelion, a perennial of the daisy family (Asteraceae) native to Eurasia. The leaves, flowers and roots are used as food and in herbal medicine, and extracts are sold as teas, capsules and tinctures.
claims: Dandelion root or leaf works as an herbal diuretic that reduces water weight and bloating.
Dandelion extract supports the liver.

name: Potassium
summary: Electrolyte balance — fix the diet (and sodium) before buying pills.
lead: Potassium is an essential mineral and the main positively charged ion (cation) inside cells. It supports nerve signalling, muscle and heart contraction, and the maintenance of fluid balance and normal kidney function. It is obtained from foods such as potatoes, beans, fruit and dairy, and is also sold as supplements and as potassium chloride medicines.
claims: A high potassium-to-sodium intake (often cited as about 4:1) reduces facial bloating.
Sports drinks and similar beverages are a convenient way to reach the potassium target.
Potassium-sparing diuretics flush sodium and water without causing re-bloating.
Large doses of potassium chloride powder are acceptable for debloating.

name: Furosemide
summary: Powerful medical loop diuretic.
lead: Furosemide, sold under the brand name Lasix among others, is a prescription loop diuretic used to treat oedema from heart failure, liver scarring (cirrhosis) and kidney disease, and sometimes high blood pressure. It was patented in 1959 and approved for medical use in 1964, is on the World Health Organization's List of Essential Medicines, and was the 29th most prescribed drug in the United States in 2023.
claims: Furosemide can be used to drop water weight quickly for a leaner look.

name: Whitening strips
summary: Peroxide bleaching that actually lifts tooth discoloration. ADA-backed, highest-confidence cosmetic buy.
lead: Whitening strips are thin, flexible plastic films coated with a peroxide gel that are pressed onto the front surfaces of the teeth for a set period, typically daily over one to several weeks, to lighten tooth colour. They are sold over the counter and are among the most widely used consumer tooth-whitening products.
claims: Whitening strips may damage teeth, so their safety is in doubt.
Using whitening strips during an isotretinoin (Accutane) course causes gum recession or discoloration.
Strips using PAP and charcoal instead of hydrogen peroxide whiten teeth effectively.
Charcoal toothpaste whitening does irreversible harm to teeth.

name: Whitening gel trays
summary: More even peroxide coverage than strips; dentist-fitted trays are the top tier.
lead: Whitening gel trays are flexible plastic trays that hold a peroxide-based bleaching gel against the teeth, usually for a period of minutes to hours or overnight. They are available as custom-fitted trays made by a dentist from impressions or digital scans, and as over-the-counter boil-and-bite or prefilled versions. The active ingredient is hydrogen peroxide or carbamide peroxide, which releases hydrogen peroxide on contact with water.
claims: Custom trays give more even whitening than strips.
A dentist-made tray is worth the higher price over over-the-counter versions.
Whitening trays make teeth sensitive and irritate gums.
Bleaching trays are harmless to enamel and other dental materials.

name: LED whitening kit
summary: The peroxide does the work.
lead: An LED whitening kit is a consumer tooth-whitening product that pairs a peroxide-based gel, applied by tray, strip or pen, with a small mouthpiece or handheld unit that shines blue or violet light-emitting-diode light on the teeth. Kits are sold over the counter as a home version of the light-assisted treatments offered in dental offices.

name: Electric toothbrush
summary: Better plaque removal and gum health than manual brushing.
lead: An electric or powered toothbrush uses a motor, or in some designs a piezoelectric crystal, to move the bristles in rapid oscillating, rotating, sonic or ultrasonic motions in place of the hand movements of a manual brush. Wikipedia classifies the devices by movement frequency as power, sonic or ultrasonic, and also by movement type, such as side-to-side vibration or oscillating-rotating heads.  Many current models add timers, pressure sensors, multiple cleaning modes and Bluetooth connectivity to a companion app.
claims: A $100 electric toothbrush is worth it over a cheap manual one.
Electric brushes give cleaner, healthier-looking teeth and gums.
Electric toothbrushes whiten teeth.

name: Water flosser
summary: Interdental cleaning and gum health — healthy gums frame the smile.
lead: A water flosser, also called an oral irrigator or dental water jet, is a home dental device that directs a pulsating stream of water at the teeth and gumline to flush plaque and food debris from between teeth and below the gum margin. The best-known maker, Waterpik, has become a generic name for the category. Countertop units with a reservoir and cordless rechargeable handhelds are both sold, with tips designed for braces, implants and bridges.
claims: A water flosser is as good as or better than string floss.
Water flossing improves gum health and reduces bleeding.
Water flossers can push bacteria under the gums or damage tissue.

name: Tongue scraper
summary: Removes tongue coating; fresher breath for a few hours.
lead: A tongue scraper, also called a tongue cleaner, is a small hand tool, typically a curved strip or loop of metal or plastic, drawn along the top surface of the tongue to remove the coating of bacteria, food debris and shed cells that can build up there. Tongue brushes and brush-backed toothbrush heads serve a similar purpose.  Tongue cleaning is less commonly practised than tooth brushing, flossing or mouthwash use.
claims: Scraping the tongue fixes bad breath.
Scraping removes bacteria and supports a healthier oral microbiome.
Persistent breath odour on low-carbohydrate diets can be handled with scraping.

name: Clear aligners
summary: Actually moves teeth and fixes bite in suitable cases.
lead: Clear aligners are removable, transparent plastic orthodontic appliances that move teeth in small steps through a series of trays, each shaped slightly differently from the last. A digital scan or impression of the teeth is used to plan the movements in software, and a new aligner is typically worn for one to two weeks and for about 22 hours a day.  Align Technology's Invisalign, which began US sales in 1999, is the best-known system; many other brands, including dentist-supervised and direct-to-consumer services, now exist.
claims: Braces cause gum recession, so Invisalign is the safer choice for facial structure.
Invisalign can expand the palate slightly while straightening teeth.
Aligners alone cannot fix a larger overbite, which needs a Herbst or Forsus appliance.
Aligners (or braces) will not fix a recessed jaw or maxilla, so surgery is needed.

name: Bruxism night guard
summary: Stops grinding from flattening your teeth over the years.
lead: A bruxism night guard, also called an occlusal splint, bite guard or nightguard, is a removable hard or soft plastic appliance worn over the teeth, usually at night, intended to protect them from the effects of grinding and clenching. Dentists make custom versions from impressions or scans, while stock and boil-and-bite versions are sold over the counter.

name: Jaw exerciser
summary: Works the chewing muscles, sure — but bigger masseters make the lower face wider, not sharper.
lead: A jaw exerciser is a handheld or mouth-worn resistance device, usually made of silicone or plastic and often shaped like a ball, bar or pair of plates, that the user bites or chews against to train the muscles of mastication, chiefly the masseter. Products in this category are sold under names such as Jawzrsize and are promoted on social media for a more defined jawline and reduced double chin.  The same term and similar devices also exist in clinical practice, where jaw exercisers are used in rehabilitation of restricted mouth opening.
claims: Jaw exercisers build a bigger masseter and a more defined jawline.
Jaw exercisers reduce a double chin or tighten facial skin.
Bigger masseters make the lower face wider rather than sharper.

name: Mastic / hard gum
summary: Masseter workout in gum form. Jawline effects uncertain, same width-vs-definition problem.
lead: Mastic gum is a chewable resin obtained from the mastic tree (Pistacia lentiscus var. chia), cultivated mainly on the southern part of the Greek island of Chios, and it is also the base of several commercial chewing gums. In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed, together with other firm or long-lasting gums such as Turkish-style hard gum and branded 'jawline' gums, as a way to give the jaw muscles resistance training in the hope of a more defined lower face.
claims: Mastic is a harder, longer-lasting chew than regular gum, so it trains the masseter better
Chewing hard gum can build a more defined jawline
Branded jawline gums offer an advantage over supermarket gum
Heavy chewing can strain the jaw joint

name: Mouth tape
summary: Encourages nasal breathing at night. Adult jaw remodeling claims: unsupported.
lead: Mouth taping is the practice of placing a strip of tape, a porous patch or a similar adhesive over the lips during sleep to keep the mouth closed and encourage breathing through the nose. It spread widely through social media, where it has been credited with benefits ranging from better sleep, less snoring and fresher breath to improved immunity, dental health and energy.
claims: Taping the mouth at night promotes forward growth of the maxilla and chin.
Mouth taping improves sleep quality and reduces snoring.
Mouth taping is a safe part of a nighttime breathing routine alongside nasal sprays.

name: Mewing appliances
summary: Marketed for palate/jaw remodeling. No adult skeletal change without real orthodontic treatment.
lead: Mewing appliances are oral devices, including palate-expanding plates, mouthpieces and tongue-posture aids, marketed to accompany 'mewing', the practice of resting the whole tongue against the roof of the mouth with the lips sealed and breathing through the nose. Mewing is named after the British orthodontist John Mew and belongs to orthotropics, his theory that tongue, lip and breathing posture guide facial growth.
claims: Mewing produces forward maxillary and chin growth, including in adults.
Mewing yields at most 1-2 mm in the teen years and mostly acts through a temporary hyoid lift.
Mewing combined with a palatal expander or MSE improves the midface.
Mewing can damage the face or teeth.

name: Red light LED mask
summary: Photobiomodulation for fine lines, tone, and texture — one of the few device categories with decent trial data.
lead: A red light LED mask is a wearable or handheld panel that delivers red light, and often near-infrared light, to the face for a few minutes per session. The technology is a consumer form of low-level light therapy, also called photobiomodulation (PBM), which applies low-power lasers or LEDs without damaging tissue. Typical marketed wavelengths fall in the red (about 620-700 nm) and near-infrared (about 700-1440 nm) ranges.
claims: Red light therapy helps acne, hair loss and many other problems, backed by thousands of studies.
Ordinary red household lights or sunlight can replace a dedicated device.
Red light does little for facial collagen, acne scars or skin, and may even age the skin.
Red light therapy treats hair loss and improves mental focus.

name: Blue light acne device
summary: Reduces some inflammatory acne lesions.
lead: A blue light acne device is a handheld wand, mask or panel that emits visible blue light, typically in the 405 to 470 nanometre range, onto acne-prone skin for several minutes per session. Clinics use higher-powered units, while consumer devices are lower in power.

name: At-home fractional laser
summary: Fine lines and texture; the strongest home-device category in the 2026 review — device-dependent.
lead: An at-home fractional laser is a handheld, low-energy, typically non-ablative device that delivers light to the skin in a grid of tiny zones, leaving surrounding tissue untouched. Consumer versions are sold for fine lines, uneven texture and mild scarring on the face, and are lower-powered relatives of clinic fractional resurfacing.

name: RF skin-tightening device
summary: Modest, real tightening with consistent use.
lead: A home radiofrequency (RF) skin-tightening device is a handheld or wearable unit that passes low-power radio-frequency energy into the skin through metal electrodes to warm the dermis. It is sold for fine lines, skin laxity and a firmer facial contour, and is a lower-power relative of clinic RF treatments.

name: Microcurrent device
summary: The "lifted" look is real — and gone by tomorrow.
lead: A microcurrent device passes very low-level electrical current, in the microampere range, into the skin through metal or gel-coated probes. Consumer versions are sold as non-invasive 'facelifts' intended to tone facial muscles and lift the facial contour, and are popular as pre-event routines.
claims: Microcurrent relieves TMJ and masseter pain and leaves the face leaner.
Microcurrent works by raising ATP, which relaxes muscle tissue.
Cranial microcurrent devices treat anxiety, depression and stress.

name: Multi-head facial tool
summary: TheraFace-type all-in-ones: the LED head has data, the microcurrent head mostly has marketing.
lead: A multi-head facial tool is a single handheld skincare device sold with interchangeable attachments, each delivering a different type of treatment. Typical heads described in product categories of this kind include LED light, microcurrent, percussive massage, cleansing, and cold or heat applicators. TheraFace-type devices are commonly cited as examples of the format. The devices are marketed as an all-in-one alternative to owning several separate gadgets.

name: Sonic cleansing brush
summary: Better debris and makeup removal than hands.
lead: A sonic cleansing brush is a handheld, battery-powered device with a soft-bristled head that oscillates rapidly to cleanse the face. It is used alongside a liquid or gel cleanser, with the stated aim of removing makeup, sebum and environmental particles more thoroughly than washing by hand. Clarisonic is commonly named as the brand that popularised the category, and many manufacturers now sell similar tools.

name: Dermaplaning razor
summary: Instant peach-fuzz removal and smoother makeup/skin surface.
lead: Dermaplaning is a form of mechanical exfoliation in which a single sharp blade is drawn at a shallow angle across the face to remove the outermost layer of dead skin cells and fine vellus hair, commonly called peach fuzz. Clinicians and aestheticians perform it with a sterile surgical-style blade, and consumer versions are small single-blade facial razors sold for home use, typically at around $10 to $20 .
claims: Dermaplaning removes dead skin cells and vellus hair for a more radiant, healthier-looking face.
Dermaplaning improves absorption of skincare products.
Dermaplaning every 1-2 weeks maximises benefit without harming the moisture barrier.

name: Derma roller (home)
summary: Professional microneedling has real collagen data. Home rolling is weak — plus an infection risk.
lead: A home derma roller is a handheld device with a rolling drum or wheel covered in very fine needles, which is rolled across the skin to create many tiny punctures. It is a consumer version of the clinical procedure known as microneedling, also called collagen induction therapy, dermarolling or skin needling . Home rollers are generally sold with shorter needles than those used in clinics, commonly in the range of about 0.25 to 0.5 mm, at prices of roughly $10 to $30.
claims: Home microneedling with a 0.5 mm roller or stamp, used consistently, improves acne scarring
Short home needles only reach superficial scarring, and longer needles are riskier to use at home
Disinfecting the roller and avoiding active acne prevents infection and worsened scarring
Derma rolling the eyebrows can help them grow, or is 'cope'

name: Gua sha stone
summary: Massage and transient fluid movement. Pleasant; fleeting.
lead: Gua sha is a traditional East Asian technique in which a smooth-edged tool is pressed and stroked over lubricated skin. In its traditional form, applied to the body for pain, colds and fatigue, it is performed until red or purple petechiae, known as sha, appear . A gentler facial version, using stones such as jade or rose quartz, has become popular in skincare, where it is promoted for contouring, de-puffing and lymphatic drainage .
claims: Facial gua sha gives a more chiselled, less bloated face
Gua sha improves circulation and lymphatic drainage
Regular use reduces fine lines, wrinkles and dark circles and improves skin elasticity
Gua sha relieves muscle tension and stress

name: Ice roller
summary: Real short-term depuff. Morning-of-event tool.
lead: An ice roller is a handheld roller with a chilled head, usually a frozen gel-filled or metal cylinder, that is rolled over the face for a short time. It is sold as a skincare tool to reduce morning puffiness and calm the look of skin and is typically priced at about $10 to $20.
